paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The Bereans were called "more noble-minded" than the Thessalonians, and it wasn't because they were smarter or richer. They "received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true" (Acts 17:11). Eager hearts and open Bibles go together, and that's the pair I want you carrying out of my bakery.

Notice what the Bereans did NOT do. They didn't shrug at Paul, and they didn't swallow every word just because he was standing there with a big reputation. They went back to the Scriptures every day, the same Scriptures Paul used when he reasoned and proved that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead (Acts 17:2-3). I check my oven timer because I've burned enough batches to know better, and checking God's Word is the same kind of smart, only it never gets old.

And friend, the Word keeps going even when people try to stop it. In Thessalonica a jealous mob stirred up the city, and in Berea the same trouble followed Paul (Acts 17:5, 13). Yet people believed in both places, and the message kept moving to a new city (Acts 17:4, 12, 15). So open your Bible with eager hands, check what you hear, and let the Scriptures stand firm under you when things get loud.
